stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 16%, and then the new price is decreased by 47%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 16% increase: $100 \times (1 + 16/100) = 116.00$. After a 47% decrease on 116.00: $116.00 \times (1 - 47/100) = 61.48$. Net change $= 61.48 - 100 = -38.52\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 16 - 47 - \dfrac{752}{100} = -38.52\%$.
